summary.text:
The meeting weighed Kafka against a managed queue for billing events. Tom noted that only per-customer ordering is needed, which the managed queue provides through message groups. Marco added that the ops cost of running Kafka is too high.

The group then discussed whether to keep the event schema in JSON or move to protobuf, and chose to stay with JSON for now.

Marco raised that an ADR needs to be written, and Priya assigned it to Tom.

Decisions:
- Use the managed queue for billing events, no Kafka.
- Keep the event schema in JSON; revisit when volume is ten times higher.

Actions:
- Tom Okafor: write the ADR for the queue decision by the next review.
summary.title: Billing events: managed queue vs Kafka and event schema format

summary.text:
The meeting compared Kafka with the managed queue for billing events. Tom said only per-customer ordering is needed, which the managed queue provides through message groups. Marco said running Kafka themselves has too high an ops cost.

The group then reviewed the event schema. Tom proposed keeping JSON for now and revisiting protobuf when volume is about ten times higher, and Priya confirmed JSON stays.

Marco raised the need for an ADR to record the queue decision, and Priya assigned it to Tom.

Decisions: Use the managed queue, not Kafka. Keep the event schema in JSON.
Actions: Tom Okafor writes the ADR for the queue decision by next review.

summary.text:
The team went through four reported issues. First was an Android crash on rotation of the payment screen, affecting about two hundred users since Monday. Lena suspected fragment state loss, and Jun took it.

Next was the slow password reset email. Tom found the mail queue worker only runs every ten minutes. They agreed reset emails should be sent immediately, and Tom will change it.

They then covered the wrong Swiss franc symbol on the dashboard, which Lena will fix, and a Safari export button report that Lena could not reproduce. Jun will ask the customer for their Safari version.

Decisions:
- Password reset emails will be sent immediately instead of through the queue.

Actions:
- Jun Park: look into the Android rotation crash today.
- Tom Okafor: change reset mail to send right away.
- Lena Fischer: fix the CHF symbol.
- Jun Park: ask the customer for their Safari version.
summary.title: Bug triage: Android crash, reset emails, CHF symbol, Safari export

Marco's on-call was quiet, with two pages that were both false alarms. Jun is testing the new build on older phones and it looks good so far.

Marco traced the false alarms to the disk alert threshold, which is at seventy percent, and will raise it to eighty five. Jun found one real bug: push notifications don't open the right screen on iOS, and will fix the deep link this sprint.

The team agreed to freeze features on the twentieth for the audit. Lena asked for someone to pair on the chart accessibility review and Tom offered to do it on Wednesday.

Decisions:
- Freeze features on the twentieth for the audit
- Raise the disk alert threshold to eighty five (Priya agreed)

Actions:
- Marco Silva: raise the disk alert threshold to eighty five
- Jun Park: fix the iOS notification deep link this sprint
- Tom Okafor: pair with Lena Fischer on the chart accessibility review on Wednesday
summary.title: Team status round, disk alert threshold, iOS notification bug and audit feature freeze

Decisions: Keep both regions active.

summary.text:
The team briefly floated ideas such as dark mode, a home screen widget and a look at analytics. Priya said none of these were planned for this quarter, and nobody took them up.

The one concrete item was the onboarding survey, which closes on the fifteenth. Jun agreed to send the results summary to the team afterwards.

Decisions:
- none

Actions:
- Jun Park: send the survey results summary to the team on the sixteenth, after the survey closes
